💡 USMNet unifies crystal-structure, compositional, and physical descriptors to predict Li-ion conductivity, overcoming sparse data and structure dependence. Small | 🔬 Research Article
💡 Fluorozirconate incorporation perturbs PS₄³⁻ anions in argyrodite electrolytes, deliberately triggering controlled decomposition to form a self-limiting, Li₂S/LiₓP- and F-rich SEI. The robust, insulating interphase enables 7000 h Li||Li cycling and 81.3% capacity retention after 1200 cycles, offering a facile strategy for durable solid-state lithium metal batteries.

💡 Hydridoborate/oxide nanocomposites achieve 3–4 orders of magnitude higher ionic conductivity via interface engineering, enabling room-temperature all-solid-state batteries. Spectroscopic studies reveal B–O bond formation and weakened M–BH4 bonds as key mechanisms. This approach yields electrochemically stable, high-capacity solid electrolytes, particularly [B12H12]2– compounds compatible with high-voltage cathodes, advancing safe, high-energy-density battery technology.

💡 This work pioneers redox-programmed bipolar membranes using electronically wired ion-insertion hosts, enabling selective transmembrane Li+ transport via coupled insertion/deinsertion reactions. It achieves a Li+/Na+ separation factor of ~2000 and demonstrates modular selectivity by swapping insertion chemistry. This bridges inorganic insertion materials with membrane separations, offering a new paradigm for selective ion transport beyond conventional polymer design.

item.title: Integration Framework for Multifunctional Hydrogel Electrolyte Modification Strategies in Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries from Molecular Design to Device Application
item.description:
این مرور چارچوب طراحی چندمقیاسی برای الکترولیت‌های هیدروژلی چندکاره در باتری‌های آبی یون روی از طراحی مولکولی تا کاربرد دستگاه ارائه می‌دهد.
Advanced Functional Materials | ⭐ Review
💡 This review uniquely frames hydrogel electrolytes as programmable, cross-scale platforms rather than passive quasi-solid media. Its novelty lies in a unified framework linking molecular interactions, network architecture, and interfacial engineering to nine regulation strategies. By bridging molecular design to wearable and bioelectronic applications, it charts a pathway from empirical optimization toward predictable, engineering-reliable hydrogel electrolytes for practical aqueous zinc-ion batteries.
🏷 aqueous zinc-ion battery · hydrogel electrolyte · molecular design · device application · multifunctional regulation
